title: NovaBridge - private deployment posture & onramp discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery for Redwood Private/VPC onramp. Customer requires private endpoints, cross-account peering, EU data residency and HSM-backed key management. Discussed options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), transit gateway patterns, NAT/egress constraints, and a short perf validation plan.
topics: VPC peering and transit gateway patterns
KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
SLA and throughput targets for dedicated capacity
next_steps: Samir to share Redwood private deployment worksheet and private endpoint guide (network diagrams)
Customer to provide VPC CIDR ranges and preferred regions (eu-west-1 primary)
Leah to propose quick perf test plan and example traffic patterns
Schedule security deep-dive with Priya and Redwood security (SAML/KMS/HSM) next week
action_items: Samir Patel - send private endpoint spec + sample CloudFormation/Terraform - due 2027-09-17
Marcus Li - export VPC CIDRs and current peering configs - due 2027-09-16
Leah Kim - draft perf validation plan and token/throughput targets - due 2027-09-20
Priya Shah - share security questionnaire and clarify KMS/HSM requirements - due 2027-09-18
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-09-14 | Start: 16:02 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Elena (NovaBridge Head of ML), Tom (Cloud Architect), Priya (Security), Marcus (DevOps)

[00:00] Samir: ok, hey everyone thanks for taking the time, this is Samir from Redwood - i'm the AE on the account, with Leah and Jordan from our solutions team. how's everyone doing?
[00:15] Elena: Good thanks, yep excited to dig in. we've been evaluating options to run inference for a subset of our customer pipelines behind our VPC. privacy and EU residency are top of mind.
[00:28] Tom: hi, quick intro: i'm Tom, cloud architect. our requirements are basically private endpoints, no public egress for inference traffic, and ability to pin model versions.
[00:40] Leah: great, that aligns with what Redwood Private supports. quick note, i'll try to walk through network patterns and what we need from your side to get a private onramp working.
[00:54] Marcus: small caveat, we do multi-account AWS - prod and infra are separate, so cross-account peering or transit gateway is a must for us.
[01:07] Jordan: okay makes sense. when you say no public egress, do you mean full blackhole outbound, or controlled egress through corporate NAT?
[01:18] Priya: controlled egress only through our NAT and egress inspection. we need traffic to traverse via our egress proxy for logging; we cannot allow direct internet to endpoints. also SOC 2 and ISO are required.
[01:32] Samir: absolutely. high level options: Hosted API - fastest go-live but that does involve outbound to Redwood's public endpoints; Dedicated - dedicated GPU pools but still public egress unless you use private link; Private - a VPC deployed instance or VPC peering with our managed private control plane and private endpoints.
[01:50] Elena: want to better understand tradeoffs on latency and cost between Dedicated and Private.
[02:02] Leah: yeah, Dedicated is our reserved capacity in Redwood-managed infra — lower tail latency for sustained throughput and simpler upgrades. Private gives you full data plane isolation in your VPC, and you control networking; tends to add some ops work and egress routing. cost delta depends on commit and whether you host in your VPC or use our private-managed instance.
[02:25] Tom: for Private, are we hosting in our account or is Redwood deploying into a cloud account you manage?
[02:35] Jordan: we support both models. "bring-your-own-vpc" is typical: Redwood will consume private endpoints inside your VPC via interface endpoints / PrivateLink, or we can peer into a customer-managed subnet with strict security controls. for some enterprise customers we also offer a managed private dataplane where the control plane is in Redwood but data plane lives in customer VPCs.
[02:58] [02:58] Marcus: sorry, interface endpoints - that's AWS Interface Endpoints (ENIs) or something custom?
[03:04] Leah: yes, interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) create ENIs in your subnet and route traffic privately. alternative is VPC peering or Transit Gateway if you want cross-account routing. for multi-account setups transit gateway is usually cleaner.
[03:24] Tom: transit gateway - any limits we should watch for? we already have some attachments for other partners.
[03:30] Jordan: TGW has route limits per attachment and some scaling considerations. we typically recommend a dedicated attachment for high-throughput inference traffic. also note MTU and path MTU discovery — large payloads like embedding batches can hit fragmentation if not tuned.
[03:49] Elena: hmm okay. on the KMS side, we need HSM-backed keys, do you integrate with customer KMS?
[03:57] Leah: yes we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM. you can supply keys and we can encrypt model artifacts and logs at rest. some customers use CloudHSM or AWS KMS with external key material. we'll need to scope the key policy and rotation model during the security deep-dive.
[04:15] Priya: good. and audit logs — where do logs live? we need to ensure audit trail for who called which model and token-level cost traces.
[04:24] Samir: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and for Private deployments we can ship audit logs to your S3 or cloud logging via a secure ingestion path. delivery method will be covered in the SOC2 questionnaire.
[04:40] [04:40] Tom: region question — we want primary EU coverage (eu-west-1) and don't want any egress to US regions. is region gating possible?
[04:49] Jordan: yes, you can pin deployments to specific regions. for Private we can provision data plane in eu-west-1; control plane communications still need to be discussed if you want fully customer-managed control plane. we also have a region routing policy to block fallbacks to other regions.
[05:06] Elena: what about model updates and rollouts? we need canary deploys and quick rollback if quality regresses.
[05:14] Leah: rollouts are supported — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a stable variant. for Private we expose the same rollout controls via API/console. the only caveat is if variants require different instance types, that can affect capacity planning.
[05:30] [05:30] Marcus: traffic patterns — our inference is bursty with short-lived spikes; what's Redwood's recommendation?
[05:37] Jordan: we recommend a dedicated pool with autoscaling and burst capacity. caching of prefixes and KV cache helps reduce per-token cost and lower latency for repeated contexts. note: transcription sometimes says "KV cash" on our docs — it's actually KV cache.
[05:53] Tom: (laughs) KV cash, nice.
[05:57] Priya: security question — SSO/SAML integration? we want SSO for Console access and RBAC.
[06:04] Leah: yes we support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. for Private customers we can integrate with your IdP; we can also configure role mappings per team.
[06:15] Elena: perfect. can you walk through network setup steps at a high level?
[06:21] Samir: quick flow: 1) We exchange network intake (CIDRs, preferred subnets, route tables) 2) Decide on pattern: PrivateLink vs TGW peering vs VPC peering 3) We provide CloudFormation/Terraform templates for endpoint creation and SG/route setup 4) We run a connectivity test, then a small perf benchmark 5) Roll pilot into production with routing policies.
[06:46] [06:46] Marcus: for endpoints we prefer Terraform. do you have examples?
[06:49] Samir: yes Samir: we'll send Terraform module examples.
[06:53] Jordan: also, if you need direct VLAN-like connectivity for on-prem, we support VPN and Direct Connect options — we've done private deployments for on-prem regulated customers.
[07:05] Tom: direct connect would be interesting for low latency, but we need to evaluate cost.
[07:10] Elena: can you comment on egress inspection — do you support forcing calls through our proxy?
[07:17] Leah: yes you can configure egress via your NAT/proxy. for PrivateLink flows, the ENI lives inside your subnet so traffic can be forced through your route tables and proxy. for peering, you'll need to ensure route propagation routes inference traffic the right path.
[07:32] Priya: and do you support mTLS between our services and the data plane? we require mutual TLS for some connections.
[07:40] Jordan: mutual TLS is supported for service-to-service communications if you host the data plane in your environment; we'll coordinate cert exchange. for PrivateLink typically the ENI handles the private connectivity and we use TLS over that path.
[07:55] [07:55] Elena: latency targets: we need p95 under 120ms for short completions in prod. is that realistic?
[08:03] Leah: for short-turn completions that's achievable with Dedicated or optimally provisioned Private capacity in the same region. Hosted could also meet it but you'd have to factor in network latency. We should run a p95 benchmark during the pilot.
[08:16] Marcus: throughput target is about 120 RPS sustained, with spikes to 600 RPS for 30s bursts.
[08:24] Jordan: sounds feasible; we'll size GPUs and batching strategy in the perf plan. we'll also recommend quantization profiles for embeddings vs generator workloads.
[08:35] [08:35] Tom: any special NAT/firewall rules? we typically block high-entropy outbound ports, only allow 443.
[08:41] Leah: 443 only is fine, but you'll need to allow the interface endpoint ENI to reach Redwood's service endpoint or the private dataplane. security groups should permit TLS from your app subnets. if using peering, update route tables appropriately.
[08:55] Priya: data retention — can you disable logs or keep minimal logs? we want to avoid storing PII.
[09:02] Samir: yes retention policies are configurable; you can forward logs to your S3 and apply lifecycle rules and encryption. also we offer redaction and prompt-level eval controls.
[09:14] [09:14] Elena: what do you need from us today to move forward?
[09:18] Samir: top items: VPC CIDR ranges, target regions (confirm eu-west-1 primary), preferred connectivity pattern (TGW vs PrivateLink), contact for security deep-dive (Priya), and a target pilot window.
[09:32] Marcus: we can get CIDRs and peering configs by Friday. pilot window — aiming for end of month if everything looks good.
[09:40] Jordan: great. regarding pilot we typically run a 2-week perf validation: smoke connectivity, then RPS stress, then quality checks against your prompt set.
[09:50] [09:50] Tom: what about pricing for Dedicated vs Private? we need a rough number for budgeting.
[09:56] Samir: i'll send a budget estimate — Dedicated is commit-based monthly; Private has additional infra/ops fees if we manage the dataplane. we'll include options in the worksheet.
[10:08] Leah: also, one gotcha: if you want full on-prem air-gapped, there are installation windows and validation steps; that's a longer project.
[10:16] Priya: that's fine, we don't need air-gapped for now — just EU-only and customer-managed KMS.
[10:23] [10:23] Elena: okay can we do a quick walk through of a sample Terraform snippet? even a high-level example would help.
[10:30] Samir: sure — i'll share after the call; we have a module that creates interface endpoints, security groups, and route table entries.
[10:38] Jordan: note on DNS - with PrivateLink you can enable private DNS so the service hostnames resolve to the ENIs in your VPC. that simplifies app configs.
[10:49] Marcus: perfect.
[10:52] [10:52] Elena: quick question — fallback behavior: if eu-west-1 capacity is saturated, will calls route to another region?
[10:59] Leah: by default we can configure a strict region policy to fail rather than fallback. otherwise we have fallback policies to route to the next closest region, but you can disable that for strict residency.
[11:15] Tom: are there any known issues with path MTU and large embedding payloads? we've seen fragmentation in other vendors.
[11:22] Jordan: yes watch for MTU; we recommend testing with your largest batch sizes. we also recommend gzip compression for embeddings payloads to reduce fragmentation risk.
[11:33] [11:33] Priya: service account permissions — what minimum IAM rights does Redwood need in our account for the BYO-VPC mode?
[11:40] Leah: minimal: create ENIs, modify route tables, describe VPCs/subnets, create SG rules. we'll provide a least-privilege policy.
[11:50] Samir: ok wealth of good questions. quick recap of decisions and open items:
[11:56] [11:56] Samir: 1) Customer prefers EU-only region (eu-west-1) and strict residency 2) BYO-VPC preferred with PrivateLink or Transit Gateway — Marcus will confirm pattern 3) Need HSM-backed KMS integration and SOC2 details — Priya will lead the security deep-dive 4) Pilot: 2-week perf validation targeting p95 < 120ms and sustained 120 RPS 5) Next step: Samir to send worksheet, Terraform module, and perf plan.
[12:28] Elena: good summary. when can we get the pilot plan?
[12:33] Leah: i'll draft and send by Monday, 2027-09-20.
[12:38] Marcus: we'll aim to provide CIDRs by Friday (2027-09-16).
[12:44] Tom: ok thanks, appreciate the walkthrough.
[12:48] Samir: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the security deep-dive.
[12:55] [12:55] Auto-transcribe note: some words may be mis-transcribed (K/V cash, etc.).
[13:02] Meeting end.
